newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi bishops lash out at widespread corruption.
newsitem.headline: Malawi bishops lash out at widespread corruption.

text.p: Malawi's seven Roman Catholic bishops warned the two-year-old government of President Bakili Muluzi on Saturday that corruption was threatening the country's peace and security.
Bishop Felix Mkhori, chairman of Malawi's bishops, read out a pastoral letter at a synod in the capital Lilongwe cautioning that Malawi was degenerating into a society that runs on bribery.
Muluzi won power in the first all-party election in 1994, ousting the country's undisputed ruler for three decades, Kamuzu Banda.
The bishops said corruption had spread to all levels of society, threatening the security of ordinary citizens.
"There is no war but there is no peace. And peace is required for the development of our nation," the letter said.
"We condemn in very strong terms, and we join all those conscientious sons and daughters of Malawi who courageously speak out against this malpractise."
The bishops also lashed out at the government's widely publicised poverty alleviation programme, saying it was more important to provide the poor with education and training than to hand out money.
"Poverty cannot be alleviated by the availability of seemingly free donations," the letter said.

Former second vice-president Chakufwa Chihana, leader of the opposition Alliance for Democracy, recently led his party in a walk-out of the coalition government with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) to protest against corruption.
Earlier this month, former Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Rolf Patel resigned over what he said was widespread corruption. He has since formed his own independent party.
